question: ______ are known as the powerhouses of the cell.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria** is known as the **powerhouses of the cell.**
 
• Mitochondria are organelles found in **eukaryotic cells** that are responsible for producing energy in the form of **ATP.**
 
• They have their own** DNA** and can **replicate themselves,** which suggests that they may have evolved from independent bacteria that were engulfed by early eukaryotic cells.
 
• Mitochondria have a **unique structure **that allows them to carry out their **function efficiently.**
 
• They are composed of an outer and inner membrane, with the inner membrane folded into structures called **cristae.**
 
• Mitochondria are involved in a range of cellular processes beyond energy production, including **calcium signaling, apoptosis**, and the **synthesis of certain biomolecules.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lysosomes** are organelles that contain **digestive enzymes**.

 
 
• They are involved in **breaking down** cellular waste and foreign substances.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes** are molecular machines that **synthesize proteins**.
 
 
• Some are located in the **cytoplasm** and others attached to the **endoplasmic reticulum.**
 
 
 
• The **nucleus** is the organelle that contains the** genetic material **of the cell and regulates **gene expression.**
 
 
• The **nuclear membrane, chromosomes, nucleoplasm,** and **nucleolus** make up the nucleus' structural components.
